Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:10:1.hebrew: ואמר להם כו' - מדכתיב "מקדש הקדשים", שמעינן דלא אסירי בתרומה, אלא מקדשי המקדש:
Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:10:1.english: And he said to them, etc. - From that which is written: “Of the most holy things,” we learn that they were not forbidden from teruma, but rather [only] from the consecrated [offerings] of the Sanctuary.

Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:10:2.hebrew: אמר להם - תרומה איני יכול לאסור עליכם, מפני חזקתכם שהוחזקתם בבבל לאכלה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:10:2.english: He said to them - I cannot forbid teruma to you, because of your presumptive status, as you were established in Babylonia to eat it.

Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:10:3.english: Consecrated [food] of the border - Teruma, which is eaten in any place.

Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:10:4.hebrew: אף כאן כו' - אלמא, מדכתיב ויגואלו, שמע מינה נתחללו מן הכהונה, והיינו חללים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:10:4.english: Here too, etc. - It follows that since it is written, “and they were excluded as defiled,” learn from this that they were profaned from the priesthood, and these are the ḥalalim.

Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:11:1.hebrew: ולמ"ד - במסכת כתובות (דף כד:):
Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:11:1.english: And according to the one who says - In Tractate Ketubot (daf 24b).

Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:11:2.hebrew: מעלין מתרומה ליוחסין - הרואה כהן אוכל בתרומה במקומו, אין צריך לבדוק אחריו ביוחסין, ונושא כהן בתו. הני, כיון דאכלי בתרומה, אתי לאסוקינהו — ואמאי לא חש לה נחמיה, דלא לאסוקינהו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:11:2.english: One elevates from teruma to lineage - One who sees a priest eating teruma in his place does not need to examine his lineage, and a priest may marry his daughter. These [priests], since they eat teruma, [people] will come to elevate them — and why was Nehemiah not concerned about this, so that they would not elevate them?

Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:11:3.hebrew: שאני התם דריע חזקתייהו - לא איצטריך למיחש להאי, דכיון דשאר כהנים אוכלים בקדשי המקדש והם נגואלו מהם — הורע חזקתם, ויש בהם היכר, ולא אתי לאסוקינהו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:11:3.english: There it is different, as their presumptive status had been weakened - It was not necessary to be concerned about this; for since other priests eat of the holy offerings of the Temple and these were excluded from them, their presumptive status was weakened and there is a recognizable distinction in them, and [people] will not come to elevate them [to lineage].

Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:12:1.hebrew: ואלא - כיון דליכא למגזר מידי, מאי "גדולה חזקה" דאמר רבי יוסי? מאי רבותא? לא היה לו לומר אלא "מנין לחזקה כו'"? מדקאמר "גדולה" — רבותא אשמועינן, דאע"ג דאיכא צד איסור השתא טפי מעיקרא, סמכינן עלה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:12:1.english: But rather - Since there is nothing to decree, what is [the meaning of] "Great is presumptive status" that Rabbi Yosei said? What is the novelty? He should only have said: "From where [is the rule of] presumptive status [derived], etc."? From [the fact] that he said "Great," he teaches us a novelty: that even though there is an aspect of prohibition now more than initially, we rely upon it.

Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:12:2.english: Rabbinic teruma - Teruma from outside the Land [of Israel].

Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:12:3.english: Teruma by Torah law - Once they came to the Land [of Israel].

Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:13:1.hebrew: השתא נמי תרומה דרבנן היא - דאכול כדמעיקרא. ומאי נינהו? תרומת פירות וירק:
Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:13:1.english: Now too, it is rabbinic teruma - that they ate, as [they did] originally. And what is it? The teruma of fruit and vegetables.

Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:13:2.hebrew: בתרומה דאורייתא - דגן ותירוש ויצהר — לא אכול:
Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:13:2.english: [Regarding] teruma by Torah law - Grain, wine, and oil — they did not eat.

Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:14:1.english: There was no [reason] to decree due to the teruma of the Land - For it was not [present] with them.

Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:16:1.hebrew: וכל זר לא יאכל קדש - כל אותו הענין מדבר בתרומה ולא בקדשים, דכתיב: ״ובא השמש וטהר ואחר יאכל מן הקדשים״, וליכא לאוקמי אלא בתרומה, שמחוסר כפורים מותר בה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:16:1.english: “And no non-priest may eat of the sacred” - That entire passage speaks of teruma and not of sacrificial offerings, as it is written: “And when the sun is down, he shall be clean; and afterward he may eat of the sacred things” (Leviticus 22:7), and it can only be interpreted as [referring to] teruma, which one who lacks atonement is permitted to eat.

Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:16:2.hebrew: ולא מידי דאיקרי קדשים - חזה ושוק של שלמים, דאשכחן דאיקרי קדשים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:16:2.english: Nor anything that is called kodashim - The breast and thigh of peace-offerings, for we find that they are called kodashim.

Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:16:3.english: From that which is set apart from the sacred things - [The] breast and thigh.

Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:1:1.hebrew: דברי ריבות בשעריך וקמת ועלית וגו' - מכאן שהמקדש גבוה מכל ארץ ישראל, דכל צדדיה סתם, וכתב: ״ועלית״:
Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:1:1.english: “Matters of controversy within your gates, and you shall arise and go up,” etc. - From here [it is derived] that the Temple is higher than all of Eretz Yisrael, as [the verse] speaks generally of all its sides, and wrote: “And you shall go up.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:1:2.hebrew: אשר העלה ואשר הביא את בני ישראל מארץ צפון - דהיינו בבל. "ומכל הארצות אשר הדחתים שם" — וכתיב "אשר העלה":
Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:1:2.english: Who brought up and Who led the children of Israel out of the north country - That is Babylonia. [And the verse continues,] “and from all the countries where I had driven them” — and it is written: “Who brought up.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:2:1.hebrew: מסייע ליה לרבי אלעזר - דנקט תנא דידן לישנא יתירא לאשמועינן, שכל עצמו של עזרא לנקות את בבל נתכוון. לפי שראה אותם שנתערבו בהן, וראה שהיו חכמי הדור עולין עמו ואין עוד בבבל שיתעסק לבדוק בהן לייחסן — עמד והפריש פסוליהן והוליכן עמו. והדור שראו הפרשתם הכירו בהם, ולא חשש שיתערבו בהן אלו הפסולין העולים. ולדורות הבאים נמי, כיון דאמר מר (לקמן קידושין דף עו:) לשכת הגזית היתה שם, ששם היו יושבים מייחסי כהונה ולויה בכל יום — מיזהר זהירי בפסולי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:2:1.english: [This] supports Rabbi Elazar - For our Tanna used extra wording to teach us that Ezra's entire purpose was to cleanse Babylonia. Since he saw that they [those of unfit lineage] had become intermingled with them [those of fit lineage], and he saw that the Sages of the generation were ascending with him and there would no longer be anyone left in Babylonia who would occupy himself with investigating them to establish their lineage — he arose and separated their disqualified ones, and brought them with him [to Eretz Yisrael]. And the generation that witnessed their separation recognized them, so he was not concerned that these ascending disqualified ones would intermingle with them; and for future generations as well, since the Master said (below, Kiddushin 76b): The Chamber of Hewn Stone was there, where they would sit establishing the genealogy of the priesthood and the levitical lineage every day — they were vigilant regarding disqualified people.

Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:3:1.english: They brought them up - Against their will.

Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:4:1.hebrew: אפרושי אפרושינהו - ומתוך שהופרשו, הכירו בהם אנשי מקומם וידעו שלא יתערבו עוד בהם:
Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:4:1.english: He separated them - And because they were separated, the people of their place recognized them and knew not to intermarry with them any longer.

Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:4:2.hebrew: ומנפשייהו סליקו - לארץ ישראל, שלא יכירו בהם:
Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:4:2.english: And they ascended of their own accord - To Eretz Yisrael, so that [people] would not recognize them.

Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:5:1.hebrew: בשלמא למ"ד - שעלו מאיליהם, ולא הכירו בהם העולים עמהם כל כך, היינו דארץ ישראל עיסה לבבל — ספק יחוס הוא אצל בבל, שנעשית בבל כסולת נקיה, ובני ארץ ישראל לא הכירום כל כך, ויש שנדבקו עמהם:
Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:5:1.english: Granted, according to the one who says - that they ascended of their own accord, and those who ascended with them did not know them so well, this is [the reason] that Eretz Yisrael is [considered] dough compared to Babylonia — [meaning that] it is of doubtful lineage in relation to Babylonia, for Babylonia became like pure fine flour, and the people of Eretz Yisrael did not know them so well, and there were some who intermarried with them.

Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:5:2.hebrew: עיסה - ספק עירובין, כעיסה זו שמערבין בה שאור, מים, וקמח, מלח, וסובין:
Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:5:2.english: Dough - An uncertain mixture, like this dough in which one mixes leaven, water, and flour, salt, and bran.

Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:5:3.hebrew: כל הארצות עיסה - פסולת אצל ארץ ישראל, לפי שבני ארץ ישראל עסוקין לבדוק ביוחסים, לפי שהכהנים מצויים שם:
Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:5:3.english: All lands are [like] dough - [They are of] tainted lineage compared to Eretz Yisrael, because the people of Eretz Yisrael are occupied with investigating genealogies, since the priests are commonly found there.

Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:5:4.english: And Eretz Yisrael is dough to Babylonia - For Ezra separated them [those of unfit lineage] and departed from there.

Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:5:5.hebrew: אלא למ"ד העלום תנן - הואיל ובעל כרחם העלום עם אלו, יצא קול פסול עליהם, והכל ידעו בפסולן, ונזהרו בהם כל העולים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:5:5.english: Rather, according to the one who says we learned "He brought them up" - Since he brought them up against their will with these [others], a report of invalidity went out concerning them, and everyone knew of their invalidity, and all the immigrants took care concerning them.

Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:6:1.hebrew: ואבינה בעם - מי היה ומי לא היה. ש"מ, לא ידע עזרא מי עלה עמו ומי לא עלה עמו, וסבור שהיו שם לוים כשרים, ולא מצא ראויים לעבודה אלא מאותן שקצצו בהונות ידיהם בשיניהם, ואמרו: "איך נשיר את שיר ה'" וגו', במזמור על נהרות בבל (תהלים קלז). שאמר להם נבוכדנצר: "שירו לנו משיר ציון", עמדו וקצצו בהונות ידיהם בשיניהם, ואמרו לו: "איך נשיר את שיר ה' על אדמת נכר?" "לא נשיר" לא נאמר, אלא "איך נשיר" — אין לנו במה למשמש בנימי הכנורות. מאותן עלו, ומן הכשרים לא מצא, לפי שהיו יושבים בבבל בשלוה, והעולים בירושלים היו בעוני ובטורח המלאכה ובאימת כל סביבותיה. והנך לויי דקתני מתניתין — מהנך דלא חזו לעבודה היו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:6:1.english: “And I viewed the people” - [To see] who was [there] and who was not [there]. Learn from this that Ezra did not know who ascended with him and who did not ascend with him; and he assumed that there were fit Levites there, but he found none fit for the [Temple] service, except from those who had cut off their thumbs with their teeth and said, “How shall we sing the Lord’s song…” in the psalm “By the rivers of Babylon” (Psalms 137). For when Nebuchadnezzar said to them, “Sing for us from the song of Zion,” they arose and cut off their thumbs with their teeth, and said to him, “How shall we sing the Lord’s song on foreign soil?” It was not said, “We will not sing,” but rather “How shall we sing?” — we have nothing with which to pluck the strings of the harps. From those [blemished Levites], some ascended, but from the fit ones he found none, because they were living in Babylonia in tranquility, whereas those who ascended to Jerusalem were in poverty, the toil of labor, and fear of all their surroundings. And those Levites that the Mishnah teaches [ascended] were from those who were not fit for the service.

Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:7:1.english: They were careful with them - He knew who went up and who did not go up.

Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:9:1.english: Great is presumptive status - One may rely upon it firmly.

Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:9:2.english: These sought the registry of their genealogy - The document of their genealogy.

Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:9:3.hebrew: התרשתא - נחמיה בן חכליה קרוי כן בספר עזרא. ובגמרת ירושלמי נמצא, שעל שם שהיה משקה למלך, היה צריך לשתות קודם, שלא יחשדוהו שמא הטיל סם המות במשקה המלך — התירו לו יין של עובדי כוכבים לשתות; לכך נקרא התרשתא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:9:3.english: The Tirshatha - Nehemiah ben Hachaliah is called this in the Book of Ezra. And in the Gemara of the Jerusalem Talmud it is found that because he was cupbearer to the king, [and] had to drink first so that they would not suspect him lest he had placed deadly poison into the king's drink, they permitted him to drink wine of idolaters; therefore he was called HaTirshata [alluding to permission to drink].

Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:9:4.hebrew: עד עמוד הכהן לאורים ותומים - כאדם שאומר לחבירו: ״עד שיבא משיח״, דאורים ותומים לא היו בבית שני:
Rashi on Kiddushin 69b:9:4.english: Until the priest arises with the Urim VeTummim - Like a person who says to his fellow, “Until the Messiah comes,” for the Urim VeTummim were not [present] in the Second Temple.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 69b:11:1.hebrew: שאני התם דריע חזקתייהו - פי' בקונטרס: במה שאין אוכלין בקדשים. ולא נהירא, דמכל מקום איכא למיחש דילמא אתו לאסוקינהו מתרומה לקדשים, ומקדשים ליוחסין. ונראה לפרש: דריע חזקתייהו לפי שבקשו כתב יחוסם ולא מצאו:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 69b:11:1.english: There it is different, as their presumptive status had been weakened - The Kuntres explained: In that they do not partake of sacrificial foods. But it is not satisfactory, for nevertheless there is concern lest they come to elevate them from teruma to sacrificial foods, and from sacrificial foods to lineage. And it appears [proper] to explain: "Their presumptive status had been weakened" because they sought their genealogical record and did not find [it].

Tosafot on Kiddushin 69b:12:1.hebrew: [ואלא מאי גדולה חזקה - בשלמא למ"ד אין מעלין, היינו גדולה חזקה — דאף ע"ג דהוי לן למיגזר דילמא אתי לאסוקינהו ליוחסין (דהא לית ליה ריע חזקתייהו), אפ"ה לא גזרי'. אלא למ"ד מעלין, דאית ליה סברא דריע חזקתייהו, מאי גדולה חזקה? הא דלא גזרינן הכא — משום דריע חזקתייהו. ת"י]:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 69b:12:1.english: ["But what is 'great is a presumptive status'?" - Granted, according to the one who says [that] one does not elevate [from teruma to priestly lineage], that is [the meaning of] "great is a presumptive status": for even though we should have decreed lest one come to elevate them to [priestly] lineage (for he does not maintain [that] their presumptive status is weakened), even so we do not decree. However, according to the one who says [that] one elevates [from teruma to lineage], who maintains the reasoning that their presumptive status is weakened, what is "great is a presumptive status"? The fact that we do not decree here is [merely] because their presumptive status is weakened. — Tosafot Yeshanim]

Tosafot on Kiddushin 69b:6:1.hebrew: ומבני לוי לא מצאתי שם - וא"ת: והא אמרי' במתניתין, "עשרה יוחסין עלו מבבל", וקא חשיב לוים? ויש לומר: דכל הלוים שעלו עמו היו קצוצי בהונות, ואינם ראויים לשורר שירה של דוכן:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 69b:6:1.english: “And found there none of the sons of Levi” - And if you say: But didn’t we say in our Mishnah, “Ten genealogical lineages ascended from Babylonia,” and it counts Levites [among them]? And one can say: That all the Levites who ascended with him had their thumbs cut off, and were unfit to sing the song of the platform.
